taxonomic_note: Accepted by Kew/POWO; native in Texas. Historical synonyms include Poa trichodes, Eragrostis pilifera, and E. trichodes var. pilifera.
look_here_first: SAND LOVEGRASS: larger arching perennial bunch with a spacious sometimes oblong fountain of very thin panicle branches bearing small pale spikelets toward branch tips. Real archived photos show a whole tuft and scale-reference tiny separate spikelets. On fresh sheaths, longer hairs often concentrate at sheath THROAT/collar (hair fringe ligule), while nodes tend smooth; this critical collar is NOT in current photos. Compare plains and bigtop by actual sheath hair location and ripe spikelets.

project_inclusion.range_basis: Hays County regional report lists sand lovegrass among natural grasses found in the Hays County study area. UT Plant Resources Center has a Williamson County field treatment. Kerr Wildlife Management Area vascular checklist includes Eragrostis trichodes.
project_inclusion.range_guardrail: Candidate seed mixes were not counted as native-county evidence.

best_field_traits: long hairs concentrated at sheath throat/collar
morphology_keys.comparison_training: Eragrostis intermedia: Usually shorter with mostly smooth sheaths and a smaller airy panicle. Eragrostis hirsuta: Hirsute across sheath surface with bearded panicle axils rather than collar-focused long hairs. Eragrostis cilianensis: Annual, coarser, glandular and many-flowered.
crew_field_walkthrough: SAND LOVEGRASS: larger arching perennial bunch with a spacious sometimes oblong fountain of very thin panicle branches bearing small pale spikelets toward branch tips. Real archived photos show a whole tuft and scale-reference tiny separate spikelets. On fresh sheaths, longer hairs often concentrate at sheath THROAT/collar (hair fringe ligule), while nodes tend smooth; this critical collar is NOT in current photos. Compare plains and bigtop by actual sheath hair location and ripe spikelets.
On the SAME mature plant, compare full sheath-body hair distribution versus throat, then actual lower branch-axil and mature spikelet with scale.
If photo lacks collar and true spikelet characters, teach genus-level ID and mark the remaining photo tasks.
morphology_keys.what_to_teach_crew: SAND = BIG open panicle, throat hairs; look for fine dangling branches carrying small spikelets. The plant can look like a transparent fountain. To confirm, check hair LOCATION (throat not sheath-wide) and the mature spikelets.
overlap_cautions: The small visible spikelets and pedicels help teach panicle parts but do not distinguish the species on their own.
The existing canonical finger-scale reproductive image does NOT depict the ligule or sheath-throat hairs; do not put an arrow claiming it does.
E. intermedia also has a very open inflorescence and throat hairs; collect comparative sheath and complete-head photographs.
what_to_photograph_for_confirmation: True collar throat hairs and ligule with mm scale
Ripe 6–10 flowered spikelets with glume attachments at 10–20×

comparisons.key_distinctions: Sand lovegrass combines a relatively tall persistent tuft, arching foliage and a large airy oblong panicle with throat-focused long hairs. Plains lovegrass is often shorter with less shaggy sheath body and a smaller panicle; bigtop typically bears more extensive sheath hairiness. Stinkgrass is an annual with coarser glandular reproductive parts. None of these is guaranteed from a lone distant view.

field_photo_quickcheck.heading: Sand lovegrass: don't stop at the giant cloud
steps: Start at the actual basal growing bunch in the new CC0 Dresden garden photograph: narrow arching leaf blades converge toward a soil-level tuft. This is NOT an excavated root crown. Then use the original Texas and Sam Kieschnick images to find the fine complete panicle and real spikelets.

BLANCO COUNTY FIELD MACRO: open the credited Cody Stricker original blade–sheath V photo. This shows the OUTSIDE junction and exactly which blade to pull away. It still cannot show the tiny white ~0.4-mm inner ligule or separately measured 4–5-mm sheath-throat hairs.

TWO real source-vouchered blade-sheath teaching panels now show the outer green sheathing culms. Neither exposes the INTERNAL 0.4–0.5 mm ciliate ligule, and the 4–5 mm sheath-THROAT hairs should not be confused with its short fringe. Peel one blade away to photograph the true ligule with a scale.
Look up-close for a pale spikelet at the tip of a fine branch.
Locate the throat/collar hairs on a different frame — they are NOT pictured in the spikelet macro.

For collar identification, the two new close-up photo panels are numbers 5–6 in the same-species gallery. They show visible lower blades and sheaths with true inner hair-fringe ligule still unexposed and unmeasured.
field_photo_quickcheck.field_rule: Use size/architecture to find the candidate; do not finalize without collar anatomy and mature spikelets.
field_photo_quickcheck.warning: The original three photographed species images now include the USDA-NRCS Texas Plant Materials Center public-domain overview (if archive succeeded) and two field views. Public-domain broad habit is not evidence for true 0.4-mm ligule fringe or lower glume. Need 10-20× collar and spikelet dissection with physical ruler. On 2026-10-26 verified original CC0 Daderot Dresden image archived and shown as in-ground bunch reference; one clearly visible aboveground crown arrow. TRUE 0.4-mm ligule, separate long throat/collar hair tuft, and exposed connected rootstock are NOT visible and remain photo gaps. October 26: added two Research Grade, individually credited blade/sheath photos with four gross arrows. The actual inner 0.4-mm ligule and separate long 4–5-mm sheath-throat hair macro remain missing; retain FIELD_READY_PHOTO_GAPS. Lane 2 2026-10-26: new regional Research Grade Cody Stricker CC BY close photograph of external blade–sheath V archived; one junction arrow added; no calibrated true ligule or whole-root connection. field_id_short_tiles.heading: 01 · LOOK HERE FIRST — TALL ARCHING BUNCH
field_id_short_tiles.short: Large perennial bunch with a very diffuse, often oblong panicle; trace the SAME flowering culm.
field_id_short_tiles.details: Kew GrassBase describes a caespitose perennial with culms about 60–160 cm and an open panicle roughly 35–55 cm long; shorter plants also occur in regional field treatments. Use the broad arching blades, attached fine-branched head and rooted tuft together. The existing in-ground cultivated garden photograph shows the crown ABOVE soil, not excavated roots. Do not identify from a distant pale seed cloud alone.
field_id_short_tiles.status: REAL HABIT PHOTOS — ROOTSTOCK/VOUCHER CONNECTION NOT VERIFIED

field_id_short_tiles.heading: 02 · HAIRY SHEATH THROAT IS NOT THE LIGULE
field_id_short_tiles.short: True inner ligule ~0.4 mm; much longer 4–5 mm hairs can surround sheath throat/collar.
field_id_short_tiles.details: UT Williamson County treatment describes a densely ciliate true ligule about 0.4 mm, with separate 4–5 mm hairs at sheath apex/collar. Peel a fresh mature blade back and photograph the INNER junction with a 1-mm scale, distinguishing its tiny ligule from long surrounding hairs. Existing Blanco County external V-junction and sheath photos do not expose the inner membrane/hair fringe; no microscopic ligule arrow may be inferred.
field_id_short_tiles.status: NEEDS_PUBLIC_PHOTO — TRUE LIGULE AND DISTINCT THROAT HAIRS

field_id_short_tiles.heading: 03 · FOLLOW FINE BRANCHES TO INDIVIDUAL SPIKELETS
field_id_short_tiles.short: Open oblong/ovate head; Kew panicle ~35–55 cm and pedicels ~5–15 mm.
field_id_short_tiles.details: Kew reports an open effuse panicle with capillary sinuous branches and solitary spikelets on fine 5–15 mm pedicels. UT Williamson reports spreading pedicels about 5–13 mm on its studied material. Follow one complete attached head and photograph actual lower branch axils, individual pedicels and mature spikelets. An airy panicle alone overlaps plains and bigtop lovegrass.
field_id_short_tiles.status: GROSS BRANCHING SHOWN — MEASURED PEDICEL/AXIL PHOTO MISSING

field_id_short_tiles.heading: 04 · MEASURE MATURE MULTIFLORETED SPIKELETS
field_id_short_tiles.short: Kew ~4–10 mm, 4–18 florets; Williamson material ~5 mm and 4–6 florets.
field_id_short_tiles.details: Photograph two or three ripe laterally compressed spikelets with a millimeter ruler, counting individual florets along one rachilla. Kew GrassBase's broad global 4–10 mm / 4–18-floret range is NOT identical to the UT Williamson County specimen treatment (~5 mm / 4–6 florets). Preserve this geographic/treatment distinction; the current source-labelled small-spikelet photo lacks calibrated floret dissection.

field_id_short_tiles.heading: 05 · DISSECT GLUMES, LEMMA AND AWNLESS TIP
field_id_short_tiles.short: Williamson: lower glume ~1.5–2.6 mm, upper ~2–3 mm; lemma ~2.6–3.2 mm, 3-veined, AWNLESS.
field_id_short_tiles.details: UT Williamson describes one-veined glumes (lower 1.5–2.6 mm, upper 2–2.5(–3) mm), a three-veined fertile lemma 2.6–3.2 mm, and no lemma awn. Kew GrassBase gives broader lower-glume 1.8–4 mm, upper 1.8–3.4 mm and lemma 2.4–3.4 mm ranges. At 20–40× separate glumes, lemma and two-keeled palea; no tiny nerve, hair or glume endpoint should receive an arrow without visible resolved pixels.

field_id_short_tiles.heading: 06 · CENTRAL TEXAS LOOK-ALIKES + PUBLIC GATE
field_id_short_tiles.short: Sand vs plains vs bigtop: compare sheath BODY hairs versus long THROAT hairs, then ripe spikelets.
field_id_short_tiles.details: E. intermedia typically has a shorter, fine open head and relatively smoother sheath BODY; E. hirsuta has more extensive sheath-body hairs and often bearded panicle axils; E. spectabilis has a broader purple tumbling cloud. Hair placement varies, so one photo or color is insufficient. NEEDS_PUBLIC_PHOTO: connected rooted Texas bunch, opened ~0.4-mm inner ligule and separate long throat hairs, whole attached panicle, lower axils, 2–3 mature spikelets dissected at scale and matched comparison sheaths. NEEDS_SITE_QA: verify seven image records, nine panels, exact individual CC/NC/PD rights, all original arrows, image identities, mobile gallery and deployment. Remain FIELD_READY_PHOTO_GAPS.
